title: Deeper top-k with a theta-filtered merge, and adaptive range size
question: (A) Does a theta-filtered merge speed up the pruned scorer at k = 100 and 1000? (B) Does an adaptive range size beat fixed 1024 at k = 10 with a similar tail?
hypothesis: (A) yes at depth, more at range size 256 and k = 1000, none at k = 10. (B) about 1.18x over fixed 1024 with a similar p99 (model of run ts-01).
motivation: GPUSparse's headline is k = 1000 (merge-dominated); Arnav's theta-filtered merge idea; run ts-01's tail at range size 256.

declared_changes.changed_test: tests/check_range_prune.py: merged-list model, checked only for scorers that report merged_lists

correctness_rule: Every configuration's top-k equals the CPU reference at its depth for every query; VERIFY=1 schedules (incl. merged lists and the switch) equal the host recomputation; prunets and prunetm schedules identical.
success_rule: A complete run under the registered protocol; reported whatever the ratios are.
failure_rule: Any mismatch or rejected expected run; ineligible processes are replaced.

runs.status: references, fixtures and smoke tests; not results
